title: Report-Supervised Vision–Language Alignment for Label-Efficient Bronchoscopic Finding Recognition
content: Background/Objectives: Fine-grained annotation of bronchoscopic findings is costly, whereas every bronchoscopic image is already described in the examination report. This study investigated whether routine report text can serve as supervision for bronchoscopic finding recognition. Methods: BiomedCLIP was aligned with the image–caption pairs of the publicly available Bronchoscopy Examination Report Dataset (BERD; 4826 training images) using standard contrastive learning, a caption-aware objective that treats identical captions as positives, and a label-aware reference. The resulting encoders were evaluated on the official test set (316 images, 180 patients) for zero-shot recognition of 23 findings, cross-modal retrieval, linear probing with 1–100% of the labelled training patients and fine-tuning, with patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals and three training seeds. Results: Alignment raised zero-shot macro AUPRC from 0.184 to 0.255–0.292 and macro AUC-ROC from 0.59 to 0.78–0.80, and reversed the effect of institution-specific prompt vocabulary. Retrieval generalised to captions never seen during training. Linear probes on aligned features outperformed DINOv2, Swin-T and pretrained BiomedCLIP at every label fraction; with 5% of the patients they exceeded DINOv2 and Swin-T trained with all labels. Caption-aware training gave no benefit over standard contrastive training, and full fine-tuning did not improve macro F1, although it improved calibration and exact-match accuracy. Conclusions: Bronchoscopy report text is an effective source of supervision that enables zero-shot recognition and markedly reduces the need for labelled images.
